metadata.title: Case-Based Reasoning: Foundational Issues, Methodological Variations, and System Approaches
metadata.abstract_summary: Case-based reasoning solves a new problem by retrieving a similar past case, adapting its recorded solution, and - if the adapted solution is validated - retaining the new case for future reuse: the four-step Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain cycle that became the field's standard vocabulary.

sections.heading: Bottom Line
sections.text: Case-based reasoning solves a new problem by retrieving a similar past case, adapting its recorded solution, and - if the adapted solution is validated - retaining the new case for future reuse: the four-step Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain cycle that became the field's standard vocabulary.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: A conceptual and survey paper: defines the CBR cycle and its terminology precisely, then reviews the methodological variations found across CBR systems implemented at the time - how similarity is computed, how adaptation is performed, how the case base is indexed and organized.

sections.heading: Evidence & Limits
sections.text:
- Definitional and taxonomic rather than empirical - its authority comes from becoming the field's standard reference vocabulary, cited in nearly every subsequent CBR paper, not from a specific tested result.
- Says little about how CBR scales to very large case bases or interacts with modern learned similarity metrics, both of which became separate later research threads.
- The Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain framing is precise enough that three decades of CBR systems still describe themselves against it directly.
